name: application-watch-progress-bar
title: Watch Progress Bar
description: Video thumbnail with a duration badge and a resume-position red progress bar overlaid at its bottom edge — distinct from progress-bars, which are standalone bars with no thumbnail/media context.
useWhen: Showing a partially-watched video in a grid or list with its resume position.
You want the progress fill computed from real watched/total minutes.
A duration badge should coexist with the progress overlay without collision.
avoidWhen: You need a standalone progress bar with no media thumbnail — use progress-bars instead.
You need full transport controls — use now-playing-bar instead.
The video hasn't been started — omit the progress overlay rather than showing a zero-width bar.
responsiveBehavior: The thumbnail maintains a 16:9 aspect ratio via aspect-video at any container width; the progress bar spans the full thumbnail width.
accessibility: The progress overlay carries role='img' with an aria-label stating watched and total duration, since bar width alone isn't announced by screen readers.
The duration badge and progress bar are positioned to avoid visually overlapping.
Title text below the thumbnail is always visible, not dependent on hover.

variants.title: Watch progress bar
variants.description: A thumbnail 72.4% watched (42 of 58 minutes), with a duration badge and computed resume-position fill, on a light surface.
accessibility: Fill width is watchedMinutes/totalMinutes, computed live rather than hand-typed.

variants.title: Watch progress bar (Dark)
variants.description: The same partially-watched thumbnail, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: The duration badge retains sufficient contrast against varied thumbnail colors via a semi-opaque black background.
